speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; can you tell me exactly where the pain travels, and does it get worse when you cough or sneeze? This helps me determine if you have sciatica or a herniated disc.

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of exercise and the radiation of pain to the foot, I need to know if you have any weakness in your foot or leg, and if you feel numbness in the area between your big toe and second toe. Also, do you have any history of spinal surgery or trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lumbar Disc Herniation (likely L5 or S1 nerve root compression).

The history of sudden onset during exercise with radiating pain to the foot is classic for a disc herniation. Given the lack of reported motor weakness or sensory deficits so far, conservative management is appropriate.
